subject: Observability ingest handshake: VPC -> Splunk HEC (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@splunk.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: infra+security@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial intake — HEC endpoint + TLS / auth details for Acme Health VPC

Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. Acme Health's security team asked us to confirm the exact handshake for forwarding logs from Redwood's private deployment inside their VPC into our Splunk Cloud HEC. They have a few constraints: no public egress (must use private connectivity), mutual TLS preferred, cert rotation window documented, and field mapping for PHI redaction checks.

Can you confirm the following so we can schedule the final handoff:
- Will Redwood run a forwarder inside the Acme VPC (container/sidecar) or will Acme pull logs from Redwood's control plane?
- HEC endpoint hostnames/ports you will target (we prefer non-standard ports if that helps firewall rules)
- TLS options: mTLS vs one-way TLS, accepted cert formats, rotation cadence, and how rotation is automated
- Throughput expectations: tokens/events/sec and batching behavior (we need to size HEC ingestion)
- Retry/backpressure behavior (how you handle bursts and what error codes you emit)
- Any trace/span context you can include (we prefer W3C traceparent propagation so traces link end-to-end)

I've attached a sample HEC schema and our recommended index mappings. If you can reply with a deployment snippet or diagram we can share with Acme's network ops.

Regards,
Alex Wu
Splunk Solutions Engineer
alex.wu@splunk.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: splunk-hec-schema-sample.json

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@splunk.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake — HEC endpoint + TLS / auth details for Acme Health VPC

Alex — thanks for the clear checklist. Looping Ben (on-forwarder/runtime) and Karthik (network handoff). High level answers below; I'll follow with a short diagram and a deployment snippet.

1) Forwarder placement: Redwood will run a small forwarder service as a tenant-managed container inside the customer's VPC (we call it the "observability-forwarder"). The forwarder has no public IP and communicates to Splunk via a peered private endpoint (we support AWS VPC peering, PrivateLink, and in some cases customer-managed NAT+IP allowlist). For air-gapped customers we can deliver an on-prem envelope that writes to a local Splunk HF.

2) HEC endpoint + ports: We recommend you provision an internal HEC listener in Acme's Splunk Cloud VPN/PrivateLink namespace. Default ports we use: 8088 (HEC) over TLS, or a custom port 8443 if your egress rules prefer. We'll accept any hostname you provide; the forwarder will be configured with the exact FQDN.

3) TLS / auth: We support mutual TLS (mTLS) and token-based HEC auth. For customers requiring mutual auth (Acme's preference), we request a CA-signed cert for the Splunk HEC and we present a client cert from Redwood. Rotation: client certs rotate every 90 days by default; we support automated rotation via a Kubernetes CronJob in the forwarder that pulls new certs from the customer's internal secrets store (KMS/Secrets Manager) or via S3-accessed bundles (for air-gapped installs we provide a signed bundle process). We accept PEM (x509) for certs and PKCS#12 on request. We'll document the rotation process step-by-step.

4) Throughput / batching: Forwarder defaults: 10k events/min per forwarder instance for typical log lines (~1–2 KB/event). The forwarder performs batching with a 200 ms max latency window and 1 MB batch size before send. For expected Acme peak: you indicated ~300 MB/day in your intake form — that maps to ~2–3k events/min; we recommend a single forwarder with an autoscaler (HPA) triggering at 70% CPU or queue depth. Ben, please confirm if we should pre-provision a second replica for burst headroom.

5) Retry/backpressure: Our forwarder follows an exponential backoff for 5xx HEC responses, with local disk-backed buffering up to 2 GB (configurable). On HTTP 429 we back off and signal queue metrics via Prometheus (metrics exposed on 0.0.0.0:9090/metrics). If persistent failures occur beyond 12 hours, the forwarder emits an alert to Redwood Console and optionally to Acme's pager.

6) Tracing / spans: We instrument the forwarder with OpenTelemetry. We propagate W3C traceparent and tracestate headers when present. We also can emit a synthesized span/event linking the original request id (if present) to the log event. For logs that contain PII/PHI, we recommend using our redaction pipeline (configurable regex-based scrubbers) before forwarding to Splunk.

Next steps: I'll attach a short diagram and the forwarder deployment manifest (RBAC + secret mount + HPA) in a follow-up, and include the cert rotation runbook. Ben — can you confirm the buffer sizing above and add any runtime constraints? Karthik — please confirm networking options (PrivateLink vs peering) that Acme prefers; I will forward their NOC the template for the peering ACLs.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-forwarder-deployment-notes.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Alex Wu <alex.wu@splunk.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake — HEC endpoint + TLS / auth details for Acme Health VPC

Marissa / Alex — quick confirmation from runtime side.

- Buffer sizing: 2 GB disk-backed buffer per forwarder instance is fine for the volumes Marissa cited. We do recommend enabling our optional compression (gzip) for HEC payloads; it reduces bandwidth and HEC ingestion cost.
- Autoscaling: HPA with CPU and custom queue_depth metrics works. Recommend minReplicas:1, maxReplicas:3 for the initial rollout. If Acme expects sustained peaks > 20k events/min we should revisit.
- mTLS details: client cert is issued from Redwood's short-lived CA; for mutual TLS we can generate CSR for Acme to sign, or Acme can supply a CA bundle. For rotation we'll dropnew certs, warm new connections, then retire old certs after 48 hours to avoid connection churn.
- Observability hooks: metrics exposed: forwarder_queue_depth, forwarder_send_rate, forwarder_error_rate, splunk_http_5xx_count. Traces: we tag spans with "forwarder.instance" and "acme.customer_id" (if provided). We'll not log full event payloads to our console — only metadata and hashes for dedup.

If that aligns, Marissa send the diagram and the peering ACL template and we'll schedule a 30-min NOC alignment call. Alex — can you confirm whether Acme wants HEC tokens rotated monthly or quarterly? They asked about token rotation during intake.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
